To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) TBX10 is a novel T-box family member that is located at 11q12-q13 and is closely linked to the BBS1 locus; and (2) mouse Tbx10 is a homolog of human TBX1 that resides at proximal Chr 1.9, a region of known conserved synteny to human 11q13.

(a) we identified a new member of the T-box developmental gene subfamily, TBX10; (b) we mapped TBX10 to human Chromosome 1 1q13 and mouse Chromosome 1.9, and; (c) we showed that TBX10 is a related but distinct member of the Tbox1 subfamily.
TBX10, a T-box developmental gene, maps to human Chromosome 1 1q13 and mouse Chromosome 1q13.2 and that it is a new gene related to TBX5, TBX3, and Tbx1.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification and characterization of genes that are involved in the development and function of the nervous system.
the development of novel methods of drug delivery to the eye.
the development and evaluation of an integrated approach to the study of the human body and its diseases, using the methods of molecular genetics.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the results of this study are in line with the hypothesis that the TBX10 gene is a new member of the Tbox family of genes.

the TBX10 gene is located on human Chromosome (Chr 11q13) and proximal mouse Chr 19 and is a member of the TBX1 subfamily of T-box developmental genes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
TBX10 is a new gene that is a member of the TBX1 family of genes, and that the gene is located at 11q12-q13 and 19p13.1-p12.1.
TBX10 is a novel member of the T-box family of developmental genes that is located on human Chr 11 and mouse Chr 19 and is expressed during development.
the human TBX1 gene maps to chromosome 22q11 and the human TBX3 gene to chromosome 12q24.1.
The main takeaway from our work is that
TBX10 is located in the same region of the mouse genome that contains Tbx1.
TBX10 maps in the same region as the BBS1 locus on 11q13, and that TBX10 may contribute to BBS.
TBX10 is an important gene that is expressed in developing and adult tissues, including the developing eye, and is a candidate gene for BBS1.
